_: Every tool that may reach the Telegram surface, and who owns it.
One entry per tool: the value is the MCP server that provides it, or
'hermes-builtin' for a tool Hermes itself provides. The per-server
tools.include lists in config.yaml are derived from this file by grouping,
so there is exactly one place a tool is declared and no second list to drift.
check_telegram_surface.py reads this on every gateway start and refuses to
start when config.yaml and this file disagree, in either direction.
Adding a tool to an agent means editing this file. That is the point.
Third-party MCP servers are NOT listed here, because none of them reach
this surface. The GitHub MCP server (32 tools) and Context7 (2) are
connected by the coding agent as a client and never by Hermes; Hermes sees
github_query, github_action and docs_query. See agents/_common/mcp_client.py.
Derived 2026-09-22 from the verified surface: config.yaml mcp_servers
tools.include, plus the three built-ins Hermes' own resolver reported
_write_tools: Tools that change something outside this machine, and must therefore be
gated by Hermes' per-tool approval before the RPC is sent.
The gate is armed by mcp_servers.<name>.trust: untrusted in config.yaml and
aimed by the readOnlyHint annotation each agent publishes: on an untrusted
server, a tool whose readOnlyHint is not exactly True needs human approval
must NOT be annotated readOnlyHint: True by its agent, and every tool NOT
listed here must be. check_telegram_surface.py enforces both directions --
a write tool that gains the annotation would silently lose its approval.
